big: Who makes sure a REIT does what it promises? Three parties: a sponsor who sets it up, a manager who runs it and a trustee who protects unitholders. And two numbers act like guard rails: 80 and 90.

lines: What stops a REIT from taking wild risks?

SEBI rules. At least 80% must be in completed, rent-earning property. At least 90% of net distributable cash flow must be paid out, at least every six months. Borrowing is capped at 49% of asset value.
